measured.dryrun: bash harness/identity/test.sh on 2026-09-03: passed 46, failed 0. conformance PASSED 16/16 against the exchange adapter with a 50-action delegation-chain corpus (actions_checked=50, missing_subject=0, short_chains=0, cyclic=0, executing_unit_mismatch=0, selected_by=configuration); the minimal call is 20 lines of caller code counted by harness/caller_lines.py and names no adapter storage; the issued credential carries three hops, current actor first, rooted in a hop obtained_via direct, with scope narrowing read:incident+call:model+write:ledger -> read:incident+call:model -> call:model and lifetimes 3600 -> 1800 -> 1200 -> 900 -> 300 seconds; a hop that widens scope is refused 403 policy-denied rule_id scope-must-narrow at platform-pre-issue with nothing issued; extending a lifetime is 403 lifetime-must-not-extend; repeating an actor is 403 chain-must-be-acyclic; an expired or self-asserted-root credential is 401 identity-untrusted, not retryable; DRYRUN_FAIL=1 returns adapter-unavailable 503; ADAPTER=live exits 2 naming the absence.
measured.swap: conformance PASSED 16/16 before (dryrun, presented-credential exchange, authority-call per verification) and 16/16 after (second, platform-fact attestation, local trust bundle) with the same 16 cases; sha256 of interface.py+call.py+conformance.py+trust.json identical across both runs (7be68c98b7300e764653c552ab5c73dd7c6514553e6fd58f4197374d69294080), so the swap was configuration; 6 axes differ (root of trust, verification locus, credential form, authority calls 153 vs 0, the declared unsupported form, the marker) while 10 contract facts are byte-identical (the chain, the lifetimes, the enforcement point, the four corpus counters, the case counts); call.py ran unchanged on both and read the same three-hop chain, with authority calls 3 vs 0; the pair run over both bindings reports adapters_run=2, selected_by=configuration, and a non-empty unsupported list for each.
measured.breakage: IDENTITY_BREAK=forward-token makes one hop forward the incoming credential unchanged instead of exchanging it for the agent actor. The exchange binding exits 1 with short_chains=1 and executing_unit_mismatch=1 over the same 50 actions, naming action-001 and the chain ['service:intake', 'user:corey'] it found; the attestation binding stays green at 0 and 0, because a document that names the unit it attested cannot be forwarded. The suite passes again once the hop is restored, so the breakage was the defect and not the run.

claimed: live mode: there is nothing to measure. PASS.md B3 records the adapter for Identity as absent and PASS.md A6 records no identity field anywhere in the system, so adapters/live.py has never reached an issuer from here

the token-exchange request in adapters/live.py: the grant type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and the subject_token/actor_token pair are sourced (X-cap-identity-002, X-cross-structure-036); the response field names access_token and expires_in, and whether a returned token's act claims can be read back into a chain, are unverified from this environment
the SVID fetch protocol behind WORKLOAD_API_SOCKET is not implemented: adapters/second.py probes the socket and returns a typed refusal rather than inventing a wire protocol it has never spoken

both standards' versions are unverified: every record on file for RFC 8693 (X-cap-identity-002, X-cross-structure-036) and for workload identity (X-cap-identity-005, X-cap-identity-007, X-gap-a-004) is a search result, not a fetched specification; docs/acceptance/matrix.json already records the standard stick as absent by owner while fetch is blocked here

chain order, current actor first and root last, is this repo's convention taken from the entry envelope and cap-identity's ActorIdentity shape; whether RFC 8693's act-claim nesting fixes that order is an open question recorded in cap-identity and not settled here

the second adapter serves delegate because it is the document-with-claims form cap-identity-implement records as an open question; an X.509 form would declare delegate unsupported instead, which this harness has not run

the scope-widening refusal is typed policy-denied 403 with rule_id scope-must-narrow because the closed registry in docs/decomposition.md 2.1.6 has no scope row; cap-mandate-broker records credential-audience-mismatch as proposed and pending registration, and this harness invents no type of its own
the trust material in trust.json is a fixture, not a key: nothing here is a real credential, and no secret of any kind is stored in this harness
